spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The numerator is first decomposed by whether neither, one, or both coefficient factors supply the prime-divisor correction. For the unperturbed piece N1, the von-Mangoldt contribution is reduced to primes, the divisor correlation is replaced by its asymptotic density, and Mertens plus Abel summation turns the remaining prime average into the kernel sin(πcv)/v. The kernel is therefore the continuous trace of the oscillatory prime shift, not an ornamental rewrite.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines the oscillatory numerator N(c), expands the two coefficient factors, and names four terms N1 through N4. For N1 it retains the prime main contribution, rewrites the d_r(k)d_r(pk) sum using a d_r(k)^2 asymptotic, applies Lemma 2, uses the Mertens estimate ∑_{p≤y}log p/p=log y+O(1) with Abel summation, interchanges integrations, and sets normalized log variables. Equation (7) is a double integral involving (1-u)^{r²-1}, f_1(u), f_1(u-v), and sin(πcv)/v.
directed.conceptual_reading: The derivation isolates a universal analytic response from the chosen coefficient profile. Arithmetic averaging supplies a scale density, while the oscillatory zero-gap parameter c survives as a sine kernel acting on a shifted self-correlation of f_1. This exposes the numerator as a structured bilinear functional rather than an opaque discrete sum.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Prime reduction, divisor-sum asymptotics, Mertens and Abel summation form a chain from the discrete shifted product a_k a_{pk} to a convolution over logarithmic scales. The variables u and v retain relative scale and shift but forget individual primes and integers.
directed.boundary_or_failure: N1 is only the zero-correction component of N(c); the enriched coefficient requires N2, N3, and N4 as well. The prime replacement and divisor correlation are main-term asymptotics with errors, so equation (7) is not an exact finite-sum identity.
directed.uncertainty: The sequence of transformations and final sine-kernel structure are explicit. Formula layout obscures some original symbols and exact factors or error exponents, so exact reproduction should be checked against the page image.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: When the correction is attached to the shifted factor pk, its divisor set is not merely the divisor set of k: the oscillatory prime p may itself enter. The identity for the divisor sum splits N3 into an inherited-divisor term that follows the N2 template and a genuinely new p-incidence term that follows the N1 template with an inserted P_1 factor.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: After reducing the von-Mangoldt variable to a prime p, the source uses, under (p,k)=1, the identity ∑_{p_1|pk}P(log p_1/log K)=∑_{p_1|k}P(log p_1/log K)+P(log p/log K). It writes N3=N31+N32 up to an error. N31 is evaluated as in N2 and gives a triple integral with f_1 and f̃_1 interchanged in the appropriate slots; N32 is evaluated as in N1 and gives a double integral containing sin(πcv)P_1(v)f̃_1(u-v). Equation (10) recombines them.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is an incidence decomposition before analysis. The shifted multiplication k↦pk changes the feature map by either preserving an old marked divisor or adding the new prime. Separating those cases identifies which previously derived kernel applies and prevents the new-prime contribution from being mistaken for a symmetric copy of N2.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The divisor-sum identity is the bridge from a correction evaluated on pk to two simpler feature channels: inherited support on k and a rank-one increment indexed by p. Each channel then maps to its corresponding continuous integral template.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The split relies on coprimality and absorbs an exceptional gcd class into an asymptotic error; it is not an exact unrestricted decomposition of the original sum. Neither N31 nor N32 alone represents the full shifted-side correction.
directed.uncertainty: Equation (9) and the two resulting integral shapes are legible, but the extracted sentence identifying which gcd class is negligible appears internally damaged. Exact error attribution, constants, and formula details require the rendered source.
